dataflow.outcome: cross-scope normalized-text read and durable provenance substitution
dataflow.sink: foreign normalized unit markdown copied into current-scope normalized objects
dataflow.source: lower-trust supplied/shared persisted task record and attacker-chosen `output_ref`

impact.why: Foreign normalized markdown can cross scope boundaries and become durable current-scope evidence/search/archive data under misleading provenance.

likelihood.why: The path requires adoption of supplied/shared task state plus a compatible readable normalized instance and victim workflow invocation.

limitations: Fresh owner-only stores reduce direct live-ledger exposure.
Random files do not satisfy normalized manifest/unit shape checks.
Automatic remote exfiltration was not established; the direct effects are cross-scope read and durable contamination.

reachability.access_requirements: control over supplied task state before adoption; no credentials, live adapter access, or arbitrary write to an already-private healthy store is required
reachability.attacker: lower-trust contributor to copied, synced, preseeded, or shared KCS task state
reachability.outcome: current-scope KCS data can include foreign markdown under current provenance
preconditions: task has current-scope `input_path` and valid hash-shaped fields
foreign normalized instance is readable and parseable
profile and incremental workflow preconditions pass
reachability.summary: The attacker needs the victim to adopt lower-trust persisted task state and must know or arrange a readable compatible normalized instance. The path is local and deterministic once the victim runs a matching incremental or retry workflow.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust contributor supplies or syncs a KCS store whose `tasks.jsonl` contains a valid current-scope task with an absolute or traversing `output_ref` pointing at another readable compatible normalized instance. When the victim invokes an incremental or retry workflow, KCS reads the foreign instance and can persist its markdown under current-scope provenance.

pub struct TaskDescriptor {
    pub task_id: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub task_type: TaskType,
    pub mode: Option<MarkdownizeMode>,
    pub input_path: String,
    pub input_hash: String,
    pub previous_raw_hash: Option<String>,
    pub parent_run_id: Option<String>,
    pub changed_unit_keys: Vec<String>,
    pub output_ref: String,
    pub unit_keys: Option<Vec<String>>,
codeEvidence.explanation: A lower-trust supplied task record controls `output_ref` alongside current-scope task identity. The field is serialized as a plain string rather than a typed contained normalized-instance reference.
codeEvidence.label: Persisted task descriptor carries output_ref as a raw string

codeEvidence.explanation: `TaskStore::all()` is the single read choke point for persisted task state. It rejects escaping `input_path` and malformed hash-shaped fields, but it returns descriptors with arbitrary `output_ref` values intact.
codeEvidence.label: TaskStore validates input path and hashes but not output_ref

codeEvidence.explanation: A schema-valid supplied record for the current `input_path` can be selected as the previous online instance. The unchecked `output_ref` is then passed directly into the previous-instance loader.
codeEvidence.label: Incremental previous-instance selection forwards output_ref

codeEvidence.explanation: The root control is missing here: `output_ref` becomes a filesystem base path without canonical containment under the current `.kcs` root. KCS reads the selected manifest and unit files with the victim process authority.
codeEvidence.label: Loader builds paths directly from output_ref

codeEvidence.explanation: After a compatible previous instance is loaded, unchanged reuse copies `previous_unit.markdown` while assigning current raw/profile/prepared metadata. This converts the cross-scope read into current-scope provenance contamination.
codeEvidence.label: Unchanged-unit reuse relabels previous markdown under the current raw hash

codeEvidence.explanation: The final sink stores the newly constructed manifest and unit objects below the current scope. Foreign markdown can therefore become durable current-scope data.
codeEvidence.label: The relabeled units are persisted in the current scope

codeEvidence.explanation: Before this read, KCS should reject absolute, parent-bearing, symlink-escaping, or semantically unbound previous-instance references and require a current-scope normalized object identity.
codeEvidence.label: Expected control: output_ref should resolve only under the current normalized root

remediation.invariant: Persisted previous-output references must identify a normalized instance contained in the current KCS scope and compatible with the current raw/profile/unit provenance tuple before any manifest or unit file is read.
regressionTests: absolute `output_ref` in `tasks.jsonl` is rejected before descriptor return
parent-traversing `output_ref` is rejected before descriptor return
`load_previous_instance()` refuses a directory outside the current `.kcs` root before `manifest.json` is read
incremental reuse rejects previous manifests whose raw hash, profile, unit keys, or prepared hashes are not bound to the current tuple
partial retry planning uses the same contained resolver as incremental reuse
remediation.summary: Reject absolute, parent-bearing, and symlink-escaping `output_ref` values at the task read boundary; resolve previous instances through a current-scope normalized-object API; and rebind loaded manifests and units to the current raw/profile/unit tuple before reuse.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that persisted previous-output references must be bound to the current KCS scope before they are used as filesystem bases. `TaskStore::all()` validates current input fields but not `output_ref`; incremental previous-instance selection forwards that string unchanged; `load_previous_instance()` turns it into a path and reads manifest/unit files; unchanged-unit reuse then copies previous markdown into objects persisted under current-scope provenance.

summary: A supplied or shared KCS task ledger can carry an unchecked `output_ref` that selects a normalized instance outside the current scope. Incremental reuse reads that foreign manifest and unit text, then can persist unchanged markdown under the current raw/profile identity.
title: Persisted task output_ref can escape the scope

assertions: `output_ref` is not validated by the task-ledger read choke point.
`load_previous_instance()` uses `PathBuf::from(output_ref)` before reading `manifest.json` and unit JSON.
Unchanged-unit reuse copies `previous_unit.markdown` while assigning current raw/profile metadata.
limitations: No real external document or live shared store was read.
An end-to-end two-root KCS runtime regression was not retained; the PoC is a local synthetic model of the vulnerable transition.
validation.method: saved V6 poisoned-state provenance, V10 static trace, and local synthetic PoC
validation.summary: The saved validation confirms that a schema-valid supplied task can preserve an absolute or traversing `output_ref`, that `load_previous_instance()` reads the selected manifest and units directly, and that incremental reuse can copy previous markdown into a current-scope normalized unit. The included PoC models this cross-scope selection and fixed containment rejection using synthetic temporary files only.
